newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM to give pep talk to business leaders.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM to give pep talk to business leaders.

text.p: Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will meet top business officials this week to discuss how to revive the economy, industry sources said on Monday.
They said Sharif was likely to use Wednesday's meeting to urge business leaders to support his debt repayment scheme and to assure them the government will be sensitive to their concerns.

"It is a very good sign because he wants to build the confidence of the business community, which was previously lacking," Ilyas Bilour, president of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI), told Reuters.
Business confidence ebbed during the three-year government of Benazir Bhutto, dismissed by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Bilour said the FPCCI had decided to cooperate with Sharif rather than demand tax breaks or other incentives.
"The federation has decided that we should not demand anything this time. Now is the time to give something to the nation and the country and we are ready for that," he said.
Sharif announced plans on Sunday to reduce foreign debt by urging overseas Pakistanis to make donations, interest-free loans and open hard currency bank accounts at home.
He also offered returns at market rates for individuals prepared to lend to the government and told foreign investors he could provide constitutional guarantees to protect their investments.
Pakistan badly needs to strengthen its foreign exchange reserves, now at about $790 million, to meet payments on its foreign debt of around $30 billion.
